title: Contributing to micropubr
text: Thanks helping improve micropubr. Bug reports, documentation fixes pull requests welcome.

title: Contributing to micropubr
text: Open issue https://github.com/daniilidisK/micropubr/issues using bug report template. Please include minimal reproducible example (ideally reprex::reprex()), built small public dataset data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq"), plus sessionInfo().

title: Contributing to micropubr
text: Never edit NAMESPACE man/*.Rd hand; generated roxygen2 (markdown enabled).
code: # Install dependencies, including Bioconductor ones (phyloseq, DESeq2, ...) install.packages(c("devtools", "BiocManager")) devtools::install_dev_deps(dependencies = TRUE)  devtools::load_all()      # load the package from source devtools::document()      # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen devtools::test()          # run the test suite devtools::check()         # full R CMD check

title: Contributing to micropubr
text: Tests use testthat (3rd edition) live tests/testthat/. Run devtools::test(), single file devtools::test(filter = "alpha"). Shared fixtures (make_test_ps(), make_da_df()) tests/testthat/helper-fixtures.R; use instead downloading data. Guard optional dependencies skip_if_not_installed("pkg"). Visual regression tests use vdiffr: vdiffr::expect_doppelganger("name", p). Snapshots stored tests/testthat/_snaps/. intentional visual change, review accept testthat::snapshot_review() commit updated SVGs. CI uploads changed snapshots artifact check fails. Test error conditions class, message: expect_error(mp_alpha(ps, group.= "Nonexistent"), class = "micropubr_bad_var").

title: Contributing to micropubr
text: One verb family. User-facing functions mp_*() verbs (mp_alpha(), mp_ordination(), …). Internal helpers start .mp_ documented @noRd. Shared argument names. Reuse existing names rather inventing new ones: object: input phyloseq object; group.(facet., color., …): metadata column names; palette: micropubr palette name vector colours; theme: ggplot2 theme (defaults come mp_set_defaults()); font.size, plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption; return.data = TRUE: return tidy data frame behind plot; interactive = TRUE: return plotly widget instead ggplot; ...: forwarded primary geom. Argument names use dot.case. Return plain ggplot (patchwork) users can extend +. Base-graphics exceptions (mp_chord(), mp_circos()) return data invisibly. Errors raised rlang::abort() micropubr_* condition class can caught tested reliably: Use rlang::warn() / rlang::inform() conditions. Optional packages belong Suggests checked run time .mp_require("pkg", "needs ", bioc = TRUE/FALSE), raises micropubr_missing_dependency error install hint. Colours must stay colourblind-safe; new palettes added R/mp_palette.R listed mp_palettes(). Follow tidyverse style guide: two-space indents, <- assignment, lines 80 characters fewer.
code: rlang::abort(   sprintf("`%s` is not a column of sample_data().", group.by),   class = "micropubr_bad_var" )

title: Contributing to micropubr
text: Fork repository create branch main. Add update tests roxygen documentation change. Add bullet top section NEWS.md. Make sure devtools::check() passes locally new errors, warnings notes. Open pull request; GitHub Actions runs R CMD check macOS, Windows Linux, test coverage, BiocCheck pkgdown build. contributing agree contributions licensed MIT licence project.

title: Getting started with micropubr
text: mp_alpha() computes within-sample diversity , grouping variable supplied, adds appropriate statistical test automatically.  Switch violins, draw rarefaction curves, plot.type:
code: mp_alpha(gp, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),          group.by = "SampleType", test = "kruskal") #> Warning: Group(s) Feces (n = 4), Freshwater (n = 2), Freshwater (creek) (n = #> 3), Mock (n = 3), Ocean (n = 3), Sediment (estuary) (n = 3), Skin (n = 3), Soil #> (n = 3), Tongue (n = 2) have fewer than 5 samples; group comparisons have #> little power and their p-values are unstable at this size. #> Warning: Sequencing depth varies 40-fold across samples; richness (Observed) #> depends strongly on depth, so consider rarefying or comparing at equal #> coverage. mp_alpha(gp, plot.type = "rarefaction", group.by = "SampleType")

title: Getting started with micropubr
text: mp_ordination() computes distance, runs ordination, draws group ellipses, reports PERMANOVA caption — default.  compositional (Aitchison) workflow one argument away:
code: mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray", group.by = "SampleType") #> Warning: Group(s) Feces (n = 4), Freshwater (n = 2), Freshwater (creek) (n = #> 3), Mock (n = 3), Ocean (n = 3), Sediment (estuary) (n = 3), Skin (n = 3), Soil #> (n = 3), Tongue (n = 2) have fewer than 5 samples; group comparisons have #> little power and their p-values are unstable at this size. #> Warning: Group dispersions differ (PERMDISP p = 0.002); a significant PERMANOVA #> may reflect differences in spread rather than in location (centroids). mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCA", group.by = "SampleType")

title: Getting started with micropubr
text: mp_taxa() shows top taxa rank collapses rest “”.
code: mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", group.by = "SampleType", top.n = 8)

title: Getting started with micropubr
text: mp_diff() visualises results DESeq2, ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC generic data frame. volcano plot generic table:
code: set.seed(1) res <- data.frame(   feature = paste0("ASV", 1:200),   log2FC  = rnorm(200, 0, 2),   pvalue  = runif(200)^2 ) res$log2FC[1:20] <- rnorm(20, 4, 0.5) * sample(c(-1, 1), 20, TRUE) res$pvalue[1:20] <- runif(20, 1e-9, 1e-4) res$padj <- p.adjust(res$pvalue, "BH")  mp_diff(res, plot.type = "volcano", label.top = 8)

title: Getting started with micropubr
text: Combine panels labelled multi-panel figure export journal column width.
code: fig <- mp_combine(   mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType"),   mp_ordination(gp, group.by = "SampleType", permanova = FALSE),   ncol = 2, tag.levels = "A" ) #> Warning: Group(s) Feces (n = 4), Freshwater (n = 2), Freshwater (creek) (n = #> 3), Mock (n = 3), Ocean (n = 3), Sediment (estuary) (n = 3), Skin (n = 3), Soil #> (n = 3), Tongue (n = 2) have fewer than 5 samples; group comparisons have #> little power and their p-values are unstable at this size. fig mp_export(fig, "figure1.pdf", column = "double", dpi = 600)

title: Getting started with micropubr
text: functions accept theme palette argument. defaults colourblind-safe, can swap freely:  See ?mp_palette mp_theme_*() family full set.
code: mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", top.n = 6,         palette = "taxa20", theme = mp_theme_nature())

title: Getting started with micropubr
text: Add interactive = TRUE plotting function get live plotly widget instead static ggplot — hover tooltips, zoom, toggle groups via legend. figure interactive plotly package installed: Interactive figures save self-contained web page via mp_export(), using .html filename: visualization gallery vignette interactive examples. Note plotly reproduce static-overlays (significance brackets), circular mp_chord() / mp_circos() figures interactive mode.
code: mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray",               group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE) #> Warning: Group(s) Feces (n = 4), Freshwater (n = 2), Freshwater (creek) (n = #> 3), Mock (n = 3), Ocean (n = 3), Sediment (estuary) (n = 3), Skin (n = 3), Soil #> (n = 3), Tongue (n = 2) have fewer than 5 samples; group comparisons have #> little power and their p-values are unstable at this size. #> Warning: Group dispersions differ (PERMDISP p = 0.002); a significant PERMANOVA #> may reflect differences in spread rather than in location (centroids). w <- mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",               interactive = TRUE) mp_export(w, "alpha.html")

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_dispersion() tests whether group dispersions (spread around centroid) differ, assumption behind PERMANOVA. Add ANOSIM/MRPP/PERMANOVA caption add.test.
code: mp_dispersion(gp, group.by = "SampleType", add.test = "permanova")

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_mantel() correlates community distance matrix distance built numeric metadata.
code: mp_mantel(gp, vars = c("pH", "Temp", "Depth"), method = "spearman")

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_varpart() partitions community variation among two three explanatory sets (vector metadata columns).
code: mp_varpart(gp, groups = list(   Chemistry = c("pH", "Temp"),   Habitat   = "SampleType"))

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_prevalence() draws prevalence-abundance scatter ("scatter") core-microbiome heatmap across detection thresholds ("core"). core taxa labelled automatically; pass color.colour points taxonomic rank handful levels (colouring "Phylum" add 60-entry legend, leave ).
code: mp_prevalence(gp, tax.level = "Phylum") mp_prevalence(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", plot.type = "core")

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_indicator() finds taxa significantly associated groups (via indicspecies). (Requires indicspecies package.)
code: mp_indicator(gp, group.by = "SampleType", tax.level = "Genus", top.n = 15)

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_run_da() tests every taxon difference groups returns tidy table mp_diff() plots. default "wilcox" method (Wilcoxon centred log-ratios) needs extra packages.
code: da <- mp_run_da(gp, group.by = "SampleType",                 method = "wilcox", groups = c("Feces", "Soil"),                 tax.level = "Genus") mp_diff(da, plot.type = "volcano", label.top = 8)

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: Leave groups every level compared reference (every pair, pairwise = TRUE). Methods known disagree, run one design look agree. "lm" fits linear model CLR values , unlike Wilcoxon test, can adjust covariates (adjust) model repeated measures (random).   consensus table behind figure available : "ancombc2" (ANCOM-BC2, corrects sample-specific sampling fractions), "deseq2" "aldex2" wrap respective Bioconductor packages installed. ANCOM-BC2 also reports taxa structurally absent group (plot.type = "zeros") whether result survives pseudo-count sensitivity analysis (robust column; non-robust results drawn open symbols).

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: Every figure records analysis behind . mp_methods() turns records methods paragraph software versions references, lists statistical caveats raised figures made – , groups small: mp_alt_text() describes figure readers see :
code: p_alpha <- mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",                     test = "kruskal") p_diff <- mp_diff(da3, plot.type = "heatmap") mp_methods(p_alpha, p_diff) #> Alpha diversity (Shannon) was estimated for 26 samples with phyloseq (McMurdie #>   and Holmes 2013). Differences among the 9 SampleType groups (Feces, n = 4; #>   Freshwater, n = 2; Freshwater (creek), n = 3; Mock, n = 3; Ocean, n = 3; #>   Sediment (estuary), n = 3; Skin, n = 3; Soil, n = 3; Tongue, n = 2) were #>   tested with the Kruskal-Wallis test (Kruskal and Wallis 1952), followed by #>   pairwise Dunn's tests (Dunn 1964) adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg #>   procedure (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995) (rstatix; Kassambara 2026). #>   Differential abundance among SampleType groups (Skin, n = 3; Feces, n = 4; #>   Tongue, n = 2) was tested for the contrasts Feces vs Skin and Tongue vs Skin #>   on taxa agglomerated at the Phylum level detected in at least 10% of samples #>   (45 taxa) using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (Wilcoxon 1945) on centred log-ratio #>   (CLR)-transformed counts (pseudocount 1; Aitchison 1986) and linear models on #>   CLR-transformed counts (Aitchison 1986). Models were adjusted for pH; the #>   Wilcoxon test cannot include covariates and was run unadjusted. P-values were #>   adjusted within each method and contrast with the Benjamini-Hochberg #>   procedure (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995); features with an adjusted p-value #>   below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change above 1 were considered #>   differentially abundant. Figures were produced in R 4.6.1 (R Core Team 2026) #>   with micropubr 0.3.0 (Daniilidis 2026) and ggplot2 4.0.3 (Wickham 2016), with #>   phyloseq 1.56.0 and rstatix 1.1.0. #>  #> References #> Aitchison J (1986). The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data. Chapman and #>   Hall, London. #> Benjamini Y, Hochberg Y (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate: a #>   practical and powerful approach to multiple testing. Journal of the Royal #>   Statistical Society Series B 57: 289-300. #> Daniilidis K (2026). micropubr: a unified grammar for publication-ready #>   microbiome visualization in R. R package version 0.3.0. #>   https://github.com/daniilidisK/micropubr #> Dunn OJ (1964). Multiple comparisons using rank sums. Technometrics 6: 241-252. #> Kassambara A (2026). rstatix: Pipe-Friendly Framework for Basic Statistical #>   Tests. R package version 1.1.0. #> Kruskal WH, Wallis WA (1952). Use of ranks in one-criterion variance analysis. #>   Journal of the American Statistical Association 47: 583-621. #> McMurdie PJ, Holmes S (2013). phyloseq: an R package for reproducible #>   interactive analysis and graphics of microbiome census data. PLoS ONE 8: #>   e61217. #> R Core Team (2026). R: A Language and Environment for Statistical Computing. R #>   Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria. #> Wickham H (2016). ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis. Springer-Verlag, #>   New York. #> Wilcoxon F (1945). Individual comparisons by ranking methods. Biometrics #>   Bulletin 1: 80-83. #>  #> Statistical notes #> * Group(s) Feces (n = 4), Freshwater (n = 2), Freshwater (creek) (n = 3), Mock #>   (n = 3), Ocean (n = 3), Sediment (estuary) (n = 3), Skin (n = 3), Soil (n = #>   3), Tongue (n = 2) have fewer than 5 samples; group comparisons have little #>   power and their p-values are unstable at this size. #> * Group(s) Skin (n = 3), Feces (n = 4), Tongue (n = 2) have fewer than 5 #>   samples; differential-abundance tests have little power and unstable variance #>   estimates at this size. #> * The Wilcoxon test cannot adjust for covariates or repeated measures; #>   `adjust`/`random` were ignored and its results are unadjusted. mp_alt_text(p_alpha) #> [1] "Box plots of Shannon, coloured by SampleType (9 categories), based on 26 data rows. Median Shannon is highest in Soil (6.57) and lowest in Tongue (3.29). Statistics: Kruskal-Wallis, p = 0.005."

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_ml() trains random forest ("rf") gradient-boosted trees ("xgb") feature table. task detected response: categorical group.gives classification, numeric one regression. (Requires randomForest xgboost, pROC ROC curves.)  two-class problem gives ROC curve --fold predictions:  numeric response switches regression, scored RMSE / R-squared:  return.data = TRUE hands back importance table fitted model, cross-validation predictions metrics attached attributes:
code: gp_genus <- phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Genus") # Which genera discriminate sample types? mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "SampleType", method = "rf",       n.features = 15, seed = 1) two <- phyloseq::subset_samples(gp_genus, SampleType %in% c("Feces", "Soil")) mp_ml(two, group.by = "SampleType", plot.type = "roc", seed = 1) mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "pH", method = "rf",       plot.type = "prediction", seed = 1) imp <- mp_ml(gp_genus, group.by = "SampleType", return.data = TRUE, seed = 1) head(imp, 3) #>   feature importance #> 1  586313 0.09609674 #> 2  295395 0.09173454 #> 3  204889 0.08663335 attr(imp, "metrics")$caption #> [1] "5-fold CV: accuracy = 73.1%, κ = 0.69"

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_coverage() draws sequencing depth across genome data frame, samtools depth, bedGraph/BED files, BAM (via Rsamtools).
code: set.seed(1) cov <- data.frame(   contig = rep(c("contig1", "contig2"), each = 100),   position = rep(seq(1, 10000, length.out = 100), 2),   depth = c(rpois(100, 60), rpois(100, 25))) mp_coverage(cov, format = "data.frame")

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_circos() assembles ideogram optional coverage, GC, heatmap annotation tracks plus weighted ribbon links. (Requires circlize.)
code: genome <- data.frame(contig = c("c1", "c2", "c3"),                      length = c(8000, 5000, 3000)) covc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genome$contig, function(ct) {   L <- genome$length[genome$contig == ct]   data.frame(contig = ct, position = seq(1, L, 50),              value = runif(length(seq(1, L, 50)), 10, 90)) })) links <- data.frame(contig1 = "c1", start1 = 500, end1 = 1500,                     contig2 = "c2", start2 = 1000, end2 = 2000,                     weight = 0.8) mp_circos(genome, coverage = covc, links = links, link.by = "weight",           coverage.type = "area")

title: Statistics, machine learning and genomics
text: mp_chord() links top taxa levels grouping variable, ribbon width proportional mean relative abundance. (Requires circlize.)
code: mp_chord(gp, group.by = "SampleType", tax.level = "Phylum", top.n = 10)

title: Visualization gallery
text: mp_alpha() computes within-sample diversity , given grouping variable, adds appropriate test automatically. x-axis labels rotate groups many long, never overlap.  Switch geometry plot.type ("box", "violin", "dot") draw rarefaction curves:
code: mp_alpha(gp, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),          group.by = "SampleType", test = "kruskal") mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",          plot.type = "violin") mp_alpha(gp, plot.type = "rarefaction", group.by = "SampleType")

title: Visualization gallery
text: mp_ordination() computes distance, runs ordination, draws group ellipses reports PERMANOVA caption default.  compositional (Aitchison) PCA workflow one argument away, envfit overlays metadata vectors:
code: mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray", group.by = "SampleType") mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCA", group.by = "SampleType")

title: Visualization gallery
text: mp_taxa() shows top taxa rank collapses rest “”. supports "bar", "area", "heatmap", "bubble" "treemap" layouts.
code: mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", group.by = "SampleType", top.n = 8) mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", plot.type = "heatmap", top.n = 10)

title: Visualization gallery
text: mp_diff() visualises results DESeq2, ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC generic table. volcano plot generic data frame:  layouts include "ma", "forest", "dot" "concordance" (compare two methods).
code: set.seed(1) res <- data.frame(   feature = paste0("ASV", 1:200),   log2FC  = rnorm(200, 0, 2),   pvalue  = runif(200)^2 ) res$log2FC[1:20] <- rnorm(20, 4, 0.5) * sample(c(-1, 1), 20, TRUE) res$pvalue[1:20] <- runif(20, 1e-9, 1e-4) res$padj <- p.adjust(res$pvalue, "BH")  mp_diff(res, plot.type = "volcano", label.top = 8) res$mean <- runif(200, 1, 500) mp_diff(res, plot.type = "ma", label.top = 6)

title: Visualization gallery
text: mp_tree() renders tree ggtree, optionally colouring tips taxonomy drawing abundance ring. (Requires ggtree/ggtreeExtra.) Agglomerating rank keeping abundant tips (top.n) keeps tree colour legend legible:
code: gp_phy <- phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Phylum") mp_tree(gp_phy, layout = "circular", color.by = "Phylum", top.n = 12)

title: Visualization gallery
text: mp_network() builds taxon co-occurrence network. (Requires igraph, ggraph tidygraph.)
code: mp_network(phyloseq::tax_glom(gp, "Genus"), tax.level = "Genus",            top.n = 40, node.color.by = "Phylum")

title: Visualization gallery
text: mp_longitudinal() shows community change time. build small synthetic time-series object demonstrate .
code: set.seed(1) n_taxa <- 12; subjects <- paste0("S", 1:4); days <- c(0, 7, 14, 28) samples <- expand.grid(Subject = subjects, Day = days) samples$id <- paste(samples$Subject, samples$Day, sep = "_") otu <- matrix(rpois(n_taxa * nrow(samples), 50), nrow = n_taxa,               dimnames = list(paste0("ASV", 1:n_taxa), samples$id)) tax <- matrix(paste0("Genus", rep(1:n_taxa)), ncol = 1,               dimnames = list(rownames(otu), "Genus")) ps_long <- phyloseq::phyloseq(   phyloseq::otu_table(otu, taxa_are_rows = TRUE),   phyloseq::tax_table(tax),   phyloseq::sample_data(data.frame(samples, row.names = samples$id))) mp_longitudinal(ps_long, time.var = "Day", subject.var = "Subject",                 measure = "Shannon", group.by = NULL)

title: Visualization gallery
text: mp_function() plots feature--sample functional table (e.g. PICRUSt2 HUMAnN output) heatmap, bar bubble chart.
code: set.seed(2) fn <- matrix(rlnorm(20 * ncol(otu), 3), nrow = 20,              dimnames = list(paste0("K", sprintf("%05d", 1:20)),                              colnames(otu))) mp_function(fn, plot.type = "heatmap", top.n = 15)

title: Visualization gallery
text: Every mp_*() plotting function takes interactive = TRUE, returns plotly widget instead static ggplot. figures live: hover tooltips, drag zoom, double-click reset, click legend entries toggle groups. requires plotly package. flag works ordinations — hover point read sample coordinates: …composition bars, segment reports taxon relative abundance hover. (interactive bars leave group.: plotly crams faceted strip labels, single per-sample panel reads clearly.) Multi-panel output (several measures, mp_combine() figures) assembled single plotly::subplot(): Save interactive figure self-contained HTML page mp_export() use static ones (just give .html name): couple caveats worth knowing. Static-annotations significance brackets drawn mp_alpha() reproduced conversion (omnibus test still appears subtitle). circular mp_chord() / mp_circos() figures drawn circlize rather ggplot2, interactive mode ignore interactive.
code: mp_alpha(gp, measure = "Shannon", group.by = "SampleType",          test = "kruskal", interactive = TRUE) mp_ordination(gp, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray",               group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE) mp_taxa(gp, tax.level = "Phylum", top.n = 8, interactive = TRUE) mp_alpha(gp, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),          group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE) w <- mp_ordination(gp, group.by = "SampleType", interactive = TRUE) mp_export(w, "ordination.html")

title: micropubr: Publication-Ready Microbiome Visualizations
text: Publication-ready microbiome visualizations one line code. micropubr unified, opinionated R package turning phyloseq object journal-quality figure single call. applies one consistent design philosophy across whole microbiome workflow — shared argument names, colourblind-safe defaults, automatic statistical overlays reproducible, auto-generated captions — every analysis, alpha diversity machine learning, produced way. Every mp_*() plotting function returns plain ggplot2 object, keep full control: just add + theme(...) layer. Pass interactive = TRUE get plotly widget instead — call, hover tooltips zoom included.

title: micropubr: Publication-Ready Microbiome Visualizations
text: microbiome figures today hand-assembled phyloseq, vegan, ggplot2, ggtree dozen helpers — dozens lines per panel, redone every paper. micropubr collapses one consistent call:

title: micropubr: Publication-Ready Microbiome Visualizations
text: One consistent interface. single family mp_*() functions shared argument names (group., palette, theme, plot.title, return.data, …) spanning diversity, composition, differential abundance, phylogenetics, networks, longitudinal data, functional profiles, machine learning genomics. Publication defaults box. Colourblind-safe palettes, clean journal theme, sensible typography automatic, reproducible figure captions every plot. Statistics built . Kruskal–Wallis / pairwise tests, PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, ANOSIM, MRPP, Mantel tests, variation partitioning indicator species analysis computed annotated automatically. Static interactive. Every ggplot-based function accepts interactive = TRUE return linked plotly widget call. Composable exportable. Combine panels mp_combine() write figures journal column widths (self-contained HTML) mp_export(). ggplot2 way . Plots ordinary ggplot objects — extend layer, theme scale like. return.data = TRUE everywhere. Every function can hand back tidy data frame (, relevant, fitted model) behind figure. Differential abundance done carefully. mp_run_da() runs Wilcoxon, covariate-adjusted linear (mixed) models, ANCOM-BC2, DESeq2 ALDEx2 one shared design, two many groups, mp_diff() shows agree. Figures write methods. Every figure records computed; mp_methods() turns methods paragraph versions references, mp_alt_text() accessible alt text. Statistical guardrails. Small groups, richness compared across uneven depths, PERMANOVA undermined unequal dispersions flagged happen. phyloseq TreeSummarizedExperiment. Every function accepts either container, mia / OMA ecosystem works box.

title: micropubr: Publication-Ready Microbiome Visualizations
text: Optional features pull additional packages demand: plotly / htmlwidgets (interactive plots), ggtree / ggtreeExtra (trees), ggraph / igraph (networks), ggalluvial (longitudinal), treemapify (treemaps), circlize (chord / Circos figures), randomForest / xgboost / pROC (machine learning), DESeq2 / ALDEx2 / ANCOMBC (differential abundance), SpiecEasi (network inference), Rsamtools / GenomicAlignments (coverage), ShortRead (FASTQ quality), qiime2R / biomformat (import) shiny (interactive explorer).
code: # Core dependencies (Bioconductor + CRAN) install.packages("BiocManager") BiocManager::install("phyloseq")  # micropubr (development version) # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("daniilidisK/micropubr")

title: micropubr: Publication-Ready Microbiome Visualizations
code: library(micropubr) data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")  # Alpha diversity with automatic Kruskal–Wallis + pairwise brackets mp_alpha(GlobalPatterns, measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),          group.by = "SampleType", test = "kruskal")  # Beta diversity: PCoA on Bray–Curtis with ellipses + PERMANOVA caption mp_ordination(GlobalPatterns, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray",               group.by = "SampleType")  # Taxonomic composition: top 10 phyla, faceted by sample type mp_taxa(GlobalPatterns, tax.level = "Phylum", group.by = "SampleType")  # Compose a multi-panel figure and export at journal column width fig <- mp_combine(   mp_alpha(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType"),   mp_ordination(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType"),   ncol = 2, tag.levels = "A" ) mp_export(fig, "figure1.pdf", column = "double", dpi = 600)

title: micropubr: Publication-Ready Microbiome Visualizations
text: Differential-abundance methods known disagree, unadjusted tests easily confounded. mp_run_da() therefore runs one several methods single shared design returns one long table (feature, contrast, method, log2FC, lfcSE, pvalue, padj, robust, structural_zero): Fold changes always log2 (ANCOM-BC2’s natural-log estimates converted), ANCOM-BC2 results fail pseudo-count sensitivity analysis counted significant unless pass robust.= FALSE. mp_diff() also reads results produced elsewhere — DESeq2, ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC/ANCOM-BC2 objects, data frame, named list consensus concordance plot:
code: gp <- phyloseq::subset_samples(GlobalPatterns,                                SampleType %in% c("Feces", "Skin", "Tongue"))  # All groups against a reference, three methods on one design da <- mp_run_da(gp, group.by = "SampleType", reference = "Skin",                 method = c("wilcox", "lm", "ancombc2"), tax.level = "Genus")  # With your own metadata: adjust for confounders, model repeated measures # mp_run_da(ps, group.by = "Treatment", method = c("lm", "ancombc2"), #           adjust = c("Age", "Sex"), random = "Subject")  mp_diff(da, plot.type = "consensus")   # which methods agree, taxon by taxon mp_diff(da, plot.type = "heatmap")     # fold changes across contrasts mp_diff(da, plot.type = "volcano", contrast = "Feces vs Skin") mp_diff(da, plot.type = "zeros")       # ANCOM-BC2 structural zeros mp_diff(list(DESeq2 = deseq_res, ALDEx2 = aldex_res), plot.type = "consensus")

what: Methods text, alt text and statistical guardrails
title: micropubr: Publication-Ready Microbiome Visualizations
text: Every figure records analysis behind : tests settings, transformations, filters, multiple-testing correction, group sizes package versions. mp_methods() turns records methods paragraph references, ready edit manuscript; mp_alt_text() writes alt text figure. figures made, micropubr also checks conditions statistics easy -read — groups smaller five samples, richness compared across ten-fold range sequencing depth, significant PERMANOVA alongside unequal dispersions (PERMDISP), method ignore covariates asked , covariate entangled grouping adjusting unstable — warns. notes listed mp_methods(); mp_set_defaults(guardrails = "caption") writes figure caption instead, "" silences .
code: p1 <- mp_alpha(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType", test = "kruskal") p2 <- mp_ordination(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType") mp_methods(p1, p2)                   # or mp_methods() for every figure so far mp_methods(p1, p2, format = "markdown") mp_alt_text(p2)

title: Plot alpha (within-sample) diversity — mp_alpha
text: Computes one alpha-diversity indices phyloseq::phyloseq object draws publication-ready box, violin dot plots, optionally annotated pairwise statistical tests. Rarefaction curves also supported.

title: Plot alpha (within-sample) diversity — mp_alpha
code: mp_alpha(   object,   measure = c("Shannon", "Observed"),   group.by = NULL,   plot.type = c("box", "violin", "dot", "rarefaction"),   test = c("wilcoxon", "kruskal", "t.test", "anova"),   add.stats = TRUE,   comparisons = NULL,   p.adjust.method = "BH",   facet.by = NULL,   palette = NULL,   point.size = 1.5,   jitter = TRUE,   theme = NULL,   ...,   plot.title = NULL,   plot.subtitle = NULL,   plot.caption = NULL,   font.size = getOption("micropubr.font.size", 11),   combine = TRUE,   interactive = FALSE,   return.data = FALSE,   verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE) )

title: Plot alpha (within-sample) diversity — mp_alpha
text: object phyloseq::phyloseq object containing count data. measure Character vector indices. "Observed", "Chao1", "ACE", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson", "Fisher", "Pielou" (evenness) "Faith" (phylogenetic diversity; requires tree picante package). group.Sample-metadata column compare across (x-axis / fill). NULL, samples pooled single group test run. plot.type One "box", "violin", "dot" "rarefaction". test Statistical test group comparisons: "wilcoxon", "kruskal", "t.test" "anova". Pairwise post-hoc tests Dunn ("kruskal") Tukey HSD ("anova"). add.stats Add significance brackets / p-values group.least two levels. comparisons Optional list length-2 character vectors specifying group pairs test. NULL, pairwise comparisons used. p.adjust.method Multiple-testing correction (default "BH"). facet.Optional metadata column facet panel . palette Palette name, explicit colour vector, NULL default colourblind-safe palette. See mp_palette(). point.size Size jittered sample points. jitter Overlay individual sample points. theme ggplot2 theme; defaults active theme (see mp_set_defaults(), otherwise mp_theme_publication()). ... Additional arguments passed primary geom (boxplot, violin , plot.type = "dot", point summary). plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption Optional labels. NULL, sensible defaults generated (e.g. omnibus test result subtitle). font.size Base font size points. combine multiple measures requested, combine panels single patchwork object (TRUE) return named list ggplot objects (FALSE). interactive TRUE, return interactive plotly widget instead static ggplot (requires plotly package). Multiple panels assembled plotly::subplot(). Note static-annotations (e.g. significance brackets) reproduced conversion. return.data TRUE, return tidy data frame per-sample diversity estimates metadata instead plot. verbose Print methods used.

title: Convert a (Tree)SummarizedExperiment to a phyloseq object — mp_as_phyloseq
code: if (requireNamespace("TreeSummarizedExperiment", quietly = TRUE)) {   counts <- matrix(rpois(40, 20), nrow = 5,                    dimnames = list(paste0("OTU", 1:5), paste0("S", 1:8)))   tse <- TreeSummarizedExperiment::TreeSummarizedExperiment(     assays = list(counts = counts),     rowData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(Phylum = rep(c("A", "B"), c(2, 3))),     colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(Group = rep(c("x", "y"), 4)))   mp_as_phyloseq(tse) } #> phyloseq-class experiment-level object #> otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 5 taxa and 8 samples ] #> sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 8 samples by 1 sample variables ] #> tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 5 taxa by 1 taxonomic ranks ]

title: Per-cycle sequence quality profile — mp_qc_profile
code: # Usually you pass FASTQ paths, e.g. #   mp_qc_profile(c("sampleA_R1.fastq.gz", "sampleA_R2.fastq.gz")) # which needs the 'ShortRead' package. Here we build an equivalent per-cycle # summary by hand so the example runs anywhere: set.seed(1) grid <- expand.grid(file = c("R1.fastq.gz", "R2.fastq.gz"),                     cycle = 1:120, score = 2:40) mu <- 38 - 0.06 * grid$cycle - ifelse(grid$file == "R2.fastq.gz", 5, 0) grid$count <- round(3000 * stats::dnorm(grid$score, mu, 2.5)) mp_qc_profile(grid[grid$count > 0, ])

title: Run a differential-abundance analysis — mp_run_da
text: Tests every taxon difference abundance levels group., one several methods, returns long, tidy table ready mp_diff(). Running several methods one call looking agree (mp_diff(plot.type = "consensus")) recommended practice: independent benchmarks show differential-abundance methods frequently disagree, adjusting confounders matters.

title: Run a differential-abundance analysis — mp_run_da
code: mp_run_da(   object,   group.by = NULL,   method = "wilcox",   groups = NULL,   reference = NULL,   adjust = NULL,   random = NULL,   pairwise = FALSE,   tax.level = NULL,   prevalence = 0.1,   p.adjust.method = "BH",   engine.args = list(),   verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE) )

title: Run a differential-abundance analysis — mp_run_da
text: object phyloseq::phyloseq (Tree)SummarizedExperiment object counts. group.Sample-metadata column defining groups. method One "wilcox", "lm", "ancombc2", "deseq2" "aldex2". Several methods run design stacked. groups Optional subset group.levels compare (least two). first reference unless reference given, groups = c("Control", "Treatment") classic two-group comparison. reference Reference level. Defaults first groups, first level group.. adjust Optional metadata columns adjust (covariates confounders age, sex medication). Used "lm", "ancombc2" "deseq2"; methods warn run unadjusted. random Optional metadata column identifying repeated measures (example subject id), modelled random intercept "lm" "ancombc2". pairwise TRUE, test every pair levels; default level compared reference. tax.level Optional rank agglomerate first. prevalence Minimum fraction samples taxon must detected tested (default 0.1, ANCOM-BC2). p.adjust.method Multiple-testing correction, applied within method contrast (default "BH"); see stats::p.adjust(). engine.args Extra arguments underlying engine, e.g. list(n_cl = 4) ANCOMBC::ancombc2(). several methods, nest method: list(ancombc2 = list(n_cl = 4)). verbose Print methods used.

title: Run a differential-abundance analysis — mp_run_da
text: data frame one row per feature, contrast method: feature (display label), feature_id (taxon id), contrast, method, log2FC, lfcSE, pvalue, padj, mean (mean relative abundance), robust (passed ANCOM-BC2's pseudo-count sensitivity analysis; NA methods) structural_zero (absent one group contrast, tested). design recorded attr(x, "mp_da") used mp_diff() mp_methods().

title: Run a differential-abundance analysis — mp_run_da
text: "wilcox" Wilcoxon rank-sum test centred log-ratio (CLR) transformed counts (pseudocount 1). Dependency-free fast, adjust covariates. lfcSE Welch standard error mean CLR difference. "lm" Linear model CLR-transformed counts adjust covariates additional terms. random, linear mixed model random intercept per level random (requires lmerTest; Satterthwaite degrees freedom). "ancombc2" ANCOM-BC2 (package ANCOMBC): log-linear model correction sample-specific sampling fractions, detection structural zeros (taxa absent whole group) pseudo-count sensitivity analysis, reported robust column. Supports adjust random; pairwise = TRUE contrasts control mixed directional FDR. "deseq2" DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test "poscounts" size factors, tolerate many zeros microbiome data. Supports adjust. "aldex2" ALDEx2 Welch's t-test Monte-Carlo CLR instances, run separately contrast. adjust covariates. "ancombc" accepted alias "ancombc2"; original ANCOM-BC superseded authors. Fold changes always log2 scale positive feature abundant first-named group contrast ("B vs " means higher B). ANCOM-BC2's natural-log estimates converted.

what: Get, set and reset micropubr defaults — mp_set_defaults
title: Get, set and reset micropubr defaults — mp_set_defaults
text: micropubr reads small set package-wide defaults every mp_*() plotting function falls back corresponding argument left default (NULL). Setting mp_set_defaults() gives every subsequent plot consistent look without repeating arguments.

title: Get, set and reset micropubr defaults — mp_set_defaults
code: mp_set_defaults(   font.size = NULL,   palette = NULL,   theme = NULL,   verbose = NULL,   guardrails = NULL )  mp_get_defaults()  mp_reset_defaults()

title: Get, set and reset micropubr defaults — mp_set_defaults
text: font.size Base font size points used default theme. palette palette name (see mp_palette()) explicit vector colours used whenever function's palette argument NULL. theme ggplot2 theme object used whenever function's theme argument NULL. NULL, mp_theme_publication() used. verbose Logical; print underlying method parameters. guardrails statistical caveats reported: "warn" (default) raises warning class micropubr_guardrail, "caption" appends "Note:" line figure caption, "" stays silent. caveats recorded either way listed mp_methods(). flag group sizes 5, richness compared across 10-fold differences sequencing depth, significant PERMANOVA accompanied unequal dispersions (PERMDISP), differential-abundance methods ignored requested covariates, covariates strongly associated grouping adjusting unstable.

title: Get, set and reset micropubr defaults — mp_set_defaults
text: mp_get_defaults() returns current defaults named list; mp_set_defaults() mp_reset_defaults() return (updated) defaults invisibly.

title: Get, set and reset micropubr defaults — mp_set_defaults
code: old <- mp_get_defaults() mp_set_defaults(font.size = 9, palette = "okabe") mp_get_defaults() #> $font.size #> [1] 9 #>  #> $palette #> [1] "okabe" #>  #> $theme #> NULL #>  #> $verbose #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $guardrails #> [1] "warn" #>  mp_reset_defaults()

title: Plot taxonomic composition — mp_taxa

Ignored cluster.samples = TRUE. cluster.samples Order samples hierarchical clustering; shorthand order.= "cluster". .label Label collapsed low-abundance category. palette Palette name colour vector; defaults taxon palette. theme ggplot2 theme; defaults active theme (see mp_set_defaults(), otherwise mp_theme_publication()). ... See mp_alpha(). return.data TRUE, return aggregated taxon--sample tidy data frame instead plot. verbose Print methods used.

title: micropubr 0.3.0
text: several methods one call (method = c("wilcox", "lm", "ancombc2")), returned one long table method contrast columns; multi-group designs: every level reference, pairs pairwise = TRUE (previously two groups); covariate adjustment adjust repeated measures random; common prevalence filter (prevalence = 0.1) multiple-testing correction (p.adjust.method); new engines "lm" (linear model CLR values; linear mixed model via lmerTest random) "ancombc2" (ANCOM-BC2, structural zeros pseudo-count sensitivity flag new robust column). "ancombc" now alias "ancombc2"; DESeq2 now uses poscounts size factors, sparse tables longer fail. mp_diff() gains plot.type = "heatmap" (fold changes across contrasts), "consensus" (agreement across methods), "zeros" (structural zeros), plus contrast, robust.top.n arguments. Multi-contrast multi-method results faceted. ANCOM-BC2 results fail pseudo-count sensitivity analysis counted significant default (robust.= TRUE, matching ANCOM-BC2’s diff_robust): confounding simulation real counts nearly ANCOM-BC2’s false positives failed analysis. named list results stacked comparison, "concordance" works single two-method result. Forest dot plots now draw top.n significant features (default 30; per panel faceted) instead every significant one, say caption many shown; legends longer list “NS”.

title: micropubr 0.3.0
text: ANCOM-BC2 results plotted intercept column (lfc_(Intercept)) rather group effect, log2 axis although ANCOM-BC estimates natural logarithms. fixed, covariate terms longer mistaken group contrasts. Results original ANCOMBC::ancombc() (whose res list tables) parsed; mp_run_da(method = "ancombc") failed reason also ignored requested reference group. ALDEx2 results plotted using standardised effect size instead log2 difference diff.btw. mp_ordination() drew ellipses groups three samples, stat_ellipse() estimate; now needs four. Composition plots (mp_taxa(), mp_chord(), mp_longitudinal()) folded abundant taxa unassigned plotted rank “”, fewer top.n taxa shown. now kept labelled deepest assigned rank (e.g. “Unassigned Lachnospiraceae”). Group-comparison p-values (Wilcoxon, t-test, Kruskal-Wallis, ANOVA, Tukey HSD) taken rstatix, rounds three significant digits micropubr adjusted printed . now computed exactly stats. PCoA axis percentages now relative sum eigenvalues, ape::pcoa() phyloseq, labels match negative eigenvalues occur. mp_dispersion() rotates long group labels, mp_taxa() wraps long facet labels instead truncating . mp_export() wrote PDF EPS file macOS without XQuartz, cairo devices used need XQuartz . now falls back Quartz PDF device macOS pdf()/postscript() elsewhere. README: mp_import_qiime2() example used non-existent argument.

title: micropubr 0.3.0
text: New mp_methods(): methods paragraph, software versions, references statistical notes, generated provenance every figure now records. New mp_alt_text(): accessible alt text micropubr figure. Statistical guardrails flag small groups, richness compared across uneven sequencing depths, PERMANOVA unequal dispersions (PERMDISP now run alongside every PERMANOVA mp_ordination()), methods ignored requested covariates, covariates strongly associated grouping (Cramer’s V >= 0.7, R-squared >= 0.5) adjusting unstable. Control mp_set_defaults(guardrails = "warn" | "caption" | "").

title: micropubr 0.3.0
text: New mp_darken() recolours finished figure dark background keeping layout. Adding mp_theme_dark() finished plot replaces whole theme, undid rotated axis labels facet strips left labels significance brackets drawn black invisible. Composition differential-abundance labels longer treat placeholders MGnify’s “Root” QIIME’s “Unassigned” taxon names. mp_methods(format = "list") now returns paragraph without software sentence, plus versions citations, figures described one time can share single software sentence.

title: micropubr 0.3.0
text: Every mp_*() function accepts TreeSummarizedExperiment (SummarizedExperiment), new mp_as_phyloseq() converts one explicitly, including row tree.

title: micropubr 0.3.0
text: Statistical equivalence tests vegan, phyloseq stats, fixture-based tests real ANCOM-BC/ANCOM-BC2 output, vdiffr visual regression tests. GitHub Actions R CMD check, test coverage, BiocCheck pkgdown site; inst/CITATION codemeta.json.

title: micropubr 0.2.0
text: New interactive argument every ggplot-based plotting function. interactive = TRUE return plotly widget instead static ggplot: hover tooltips, zoom/pan legend toggling, ggplot subtitle caption preserved. Multi-panel output (multiple measures mp_combine() figures) assembled single plotly::subplot() deduplicated shared legend. Supported mp_alpha(), mp_ordination(), mp_taxa(), mp_diff(), mp_longitudinal(), mp_function(), mp_network(), mp_tree(), mp_dispersion(), mp_mantel(), mp_varpart(), mp_prevalence(), mp_indicator(), mp_ml() mp_combine(). circular circlize-based figures (mp_chord(), mp_circos(), mp_coverage()) ggplots interactive mode. Requires new (suggested) plotly package. New mp_qc_profile(): per-cycle FASTQ read-quality profiles (diagnostic used pick DADA2/QIIME 2 truncation lengths) frequency heatmap mean ± inter-quartile ribbon, mean/quartile overlays Q-score reference line. Reads FASTQ via lightweight ShortRead backend, accepts pre-computed per-cycle data frame, supports interactive return.data like rest family. mp_export() now saves interactive widget self-contained .html page (via htmlwidgets) given one. vignettes gained live “Interactive figures” section. New mp_ml(): supervised machine learning (random forest xgboost) microbiome classification regression, k-fold cross-validation "importance", "roc", "confusion" "prediction" plots. Like functions returns tidy importance table (fitted model performance metrics attached) return.data = TRUE. New mp_chord(): chord diagram linking top taxa levels grouping variable (via circlize). mp_circos() gained colour/weight-mapped links (link.), multi-sample coverage tracks, real heatmap track, feature-type annotation colours (annotation.), configurable track heights optional legend. x-axis tick labels now rotate automatically categories many long (mp_alpha(), mp_longitudinal()), longer overlap. mp_tree() longer prints harmless “one class ‘phylo’ cache” diagnostic emitted phyloseq tidytree/ggtree loaded together. Two new vignettes: “Visualization gallery” “Statistics, machine learning genomics”.

title: micropubr 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Core plotting family: mp_alpha(), mp_ordination(), mp_taxa(), mp_diff(), mp_tree(), mp_network(), mp_longitudinal() mp_function(). Infrastructure: mp_palette(), mp_theme_*() family, mp_combine(), mp_export(), mp_import_*() helpers interactive mp_explore() Shiny gadget. Colourblind-safe default palettes clean publication theme applied across functions. Automatic statistical overlays (pairwise tests, PERMANOVA) reproducible, auto-generated figure captions.
